The contrast is a task-evoked, whole-brain decision-making contrast relating to uncertainty in choices (50% vs other probabilities). It fits the broad common decision-making category (covers ambiguous decision-making) and meets global task/map requirements.

The primary contrast compares the pure uncertainty (50% equal-probability) condition to other probabilistic conditions (50% vs others). According to the subtype rule, 50/50 guessing or equal-probability choices map to ambiguous decision-making, and the contrast is high-uncertainty > lower-uncertainty, satisfying ambiguous inclusion criteria.

Excluded because this contrast indexes probability/uncertainty (50% vs other probabilities) rather than sensory/perceptual evidence; it therefore meets PERCEPTUAL_DM_E1 (exclude economic/probability uncertainty contrasts).
